thread:
Marissa Cole: putting together the exec readout for Unit Econ dashboard v1. need to align on what we can confidently say vs caveats. esp re: “blended $/1M output tokens” + drilldowns. pls drop any wording you want in the deck / anything we should avoid.

Talia Benson: +1. goal is to avoid execs repeating a number that later changes b/c of backfill or rate card updates. hoping we can land on a “safe claims” section + “known limitations (v1)” slide.

Rishi Malhotra: from FP&A POV, we can say:
- metric is *blended* cost, based on the 2025Q4 GPU rate card + allocation methodology v1.
- reconciles to infra spend *within agreed tolerance* at the monthly level once the reconciliation report is run.
Caveats to include:
- not marginal cost; doesn’t represent “cost to serve one more token.”
- rate card updates are versioned; numbers can move when the rate card version changes.
- partial periods (last 24h) are subject to pipeline lag.

Laura Bennett: pls make sure wording says “finance-aligned definition” not “finance audited.” also: we should explicitly call out that idle capacity treatment is an allocation choice (not an error) so we don’t trigger an idle-capacity debate in the readout.

Marissa Cole: noted. “finance-aligned, methodology v1” is good.

Logan Wright: reliability-wise, what’s “safe” today:
- trends directionally at the overall level, and model-level for hosted traffic is solid.
- region drilldown is good *after* normalization; still some “unknown” bucket from legacy labels.
Caveats:
- some dedicated/private flows still missing tier label in historical backfill → coverage improving but not 100% for older weeks.
- hourly freshness is typically <2h but can slip during warehouse maintenance/backfills.

Nadia Rahman: on token metering: we fixed the streaming undercount path last week but rollout wasn’t instantaneous.
Suggested caveat text: “For dates prior to <rollout date>, streaming workloads may under-report output tokens in some routes; use weekly/monthly views for executive reporting.”
Also: tool-calls / truncation edge cases are now covered by regression tests, but I’d avoid promising “perfect parity” wording.

Dylan Brooks: +1 to avoiding “perfect.”
I’d frame exec takeaway as: dashboard is now our *single place* to see unit cost drivers + regressions, and we have SLOs/alerts around data freshness/completeness.
But do NOT let this become “we now know exact profitability per customer/model.”
Also: please don’t show any top-N table that could be reverse-mapped to a specific customer or deal.

Alicia Perez: re: messaging + UX caveats: we should say the chart is “blended $/1M output tokens (lower is better)” and always show confidence/coverage indicator if a filter selection has incomplete dimension coverage.
Also recommend a note on rounding: we’re rounding to nearest $0.01 per 1M tokens for exec slides to avoid noise discussions.

Allison Grant: for the readout, can we include the SLO statement in plain english:
- “Data is expected to be complete hourly with up to 2 hours delay; if completeness drops, SRE + Telemetry are paged.”
And caveat:
- “During backfills, drilldown queries can be slower and last 24h may be less stable.”

Aditya Rao: for Optimize leadership, the safe claim is: “we can attribute changes to batching/cache/quant profile signals at an aggregate level and identify the biggest drivers.”
Caveat: these are *contributing signals* not a causal proof. i.e., cache hit rate correlates w cost but isn’t the only factor.

Marissa Cole: super helpful. i’m drafting a slide w:

SAFE TO SAY (v1)
1) “Blended $/1M output tokens” is finance-aligned (methodology v1) + reconciles to infra spend via monthly reconciliation report.
2) Trends + deltas are reliable for overall + model-level (hosted), with drilldowns by model/region/tier where coverage indicator is green.
3) We can diagnose key drivers via cache hit rate, batching efficiency, avg output length, streaming flag, quant profile.
4) We have freshness/completeness SLOs + alerting/oncall.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS / CAVEATS
a) metric is blended allocation, not marginal.
b) last 24h subject to pipeline lag; recommend weekly+ windows for exec reporting.
c) historical data may shift due to backfills + tier/region normalization.
d) streaming undercount may affect pre-rollout periods for some routes.
e) rate card versions can shift levels; trends should be compared within same rate card.

Anything missing / wording you dislike?

Rishi Malhotra: add: “compare apples-to-apples within same methodology + rate card version.” and explicitly call out timezone/day-boundary: finance uses UTC day boundary for now (until we land finance-local view).

Laura Bennett: yes, and please add “do not use customer-level views for exec materials” (even internal). aggregated only.

Logan Wright: we should also call out “unknown” region bucket: “<X% of traffic may appear as Unknown region while legacy mapping is retired; this is monitored.” we can put actual % from latest run.

Nadia Rahman: +1, and for streaming caveat include a crisp date: “prior to Feb 3” (or whatever rollout date you put). otherwise it reads like an indefinite problem.

Allison Grant: on SLO language: avoid numbers that we might tweak next week. “within a few hours” + “alerted automatically” is safer than “2 hours” unless we’re committed.

Dylan Brooks: agree w Allison. execs will cling to 2h.
Suggest: “Near-real-time (hourly) with a short delay; exceptions are alerted.”

Talia Benson: action item: Marissa, can you ping me the exact caveat copy you want? I’ll make sure it matches what we’re communicating in the go/no-go thread + launch checklist.

Marissa Cole: yep. i’ll update slide copy w “near-real-time (hourly) with short delay” + include specific rollout date for streaming fix. will also add “Unknown region bucket monitored; target <1%.”

Alicia Perez: can you also add a speaker note: “When coverage indicator is yellow/red, do not quote absolute levels; use trend direction or broaden filters.”

Marissa Cole: good call. adding.

Laura Bennett: final note: please say “directionally reliable for decision-making” not “accurate.” accuracy turns into audit language.

Marissa Cole: :thumbsup: will use “finance-aligned + operationally reliable” wording.

Talia Benson: thanks all. once Marissa updates deck, I’ll schedule 15m tomorrow for final exec messaging sign-off w FP&A + Eng sponsor.
